_strings.@@f8ee92abd16a: Tuition and Textbook Credit (K-12) — A parent/taxpayer who claims a dependent attending grades K-12 at an accredited Iowa school (or receiving qualifying private instruction under Iowa Code 422.12) and who paid tuition and textbook expenses for that dependent. Purchases made from Students First Educational Savings Account (ESA) funds are NOT eligible.
_strings.@@fcab89219412: Treaty conformity — IA conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from IA income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the IA return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Iowa conforms. The 2025 IA 1040 keeps the redesign's starting point — "federal taxable income" — with Step 4 computing Iowa taxable income as federal taxable income (IA 1040 line 2, from federal 1040 line 15) plus net Iowa modifications from IA 1040 Schedule 1 (line 3, from Schedule 1 line 21). Lines 1a-1f (federal total income, adjustments, AGI, standard/itemized deduction, QBI deduction, and — new for 2025 — the federal senior deduction) are printed for reference only ("Do not include lines 1a through 1f"). Iowa applies rolling IRC conformity. Federally treaty-exempt income is excluded from federal AGI/federal taxable income before it ever reaches the Iowa return, and there is NO treaty/foreign-income re-inclusion among the Schedule 1 Column A additions. Reinforced by Iowa Admin. Code rule 701—300.17 (a resident is taxed on all income "except when an item of income is specifically exempted from taxation by a provision of federal or Iowa law"). Therefore treaty-exempt income is not re-taxed.
_strings.@@fd4d92a7a276: Low-Income Exemption (with elevated threshold for filers age 65+) — An exemption from Iowa income tax (not a dollar credit) functioning as Iowa's primary low-income and senior relief. A taxpayer is exempt from Iowa income tax if Iowa taxable income (IA 1040 line 4, with required add-backs) is at or below the threshold for their filing status. NEW for 2025 — the federal 'Enhanced Deduction for Seniors' is treated as a personal exemption that must be ADDED BACK when calculating the low-income exemption.

state_tax.work_common_tail: 0. Tax line: IA 1040 (41-001) Step 5, line 5: 'Iowa tax. Multiply line 4 by 3.8% or amount from alternate tax calculation' — computed on IA 1040 line 4 'Iowa taxable income' (line 4 = line 2 federal taxable income + line 3 net Iowa modifications; 'Do not include lines 1a through 1f'). This op computes the state's flat-rate tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: 2025 STRUCTURAL CHANGE (SF 2442, enacted May 2024): Iowa went FLAT. The three 2024 brackets (4.40%/4.82%/5.70%) are GONE — for tax years beginning on or after 1/1/2025 there is a SINGLE flat rate of 3.8% on Iowa taxable income (IA 1040 line 5 = line 4 x 3.8%). Do NOT apply 2024 bracket figures to 2025, and do NOT use this pack for 2024. Base guidance: supply 2025 IA 1040 line 4 'Iowa taxable income' = line 2 federal taxable income (federal 1040, line 15) + line 3 net Iowa modifications (IA 1040 Schedule 1, line 21). Lines 1a-1f (federal total income, adjustments, AGI, standard/itemized deduction, QBI deduction, and — new for 2025 — the federal senior deduction) are printed for reference only. The federal standard/itemized and QBI deductions are already inside federal taxable income — Iowa has no state standard deduction or base personal exemptions, so this op subtracts nothing before applying the 3.8% rate (standard_deduction is null; exemptions is empty). Flat rate makes filing status irrelevant to line 5: with a single 3.8% rate and no per-status standard deduction, single / MFS / HoH / MFJ all compute the identical tax on the same base. The op's qualifying-surviving-spouse -> married_filing_jointly aliasing (which was a CRITICAL understatement warning in the 2024 graduated pack, since Iowa status 5 is NON-JOINT on the bracket worksheet) is now HARMLESS — the flat rate is status-independent. It matters only for the ALTERNATE tax (off-model, below). Alternate tax (NOT modeled) survives for 2025 at a REDUCED rate: all statuses except single may compute an alternate tax on the 2025 IA 1040 Alternate Tax Worksheet (41-145) — 4.3% (.043), DOWN from 5.7% in 2024 — of income above $13,500 ($32,000 if you or your spouse was 65 or older on 12/31/2025), and enter the SMALLER of that or 3.8% x line 4 on line 5 (check the Step 5 box). Status-3 (MFS) spouses prorate it. This provision is REPEALED for tax years beginning on or after 1/1/2026. Single taxpayers may instead qualify for the Iowa Income Tax Reduction Worksheet (41-146). Check these when income is just above the threshold. Exemption CREDITS, not base exemptions (NOT modeled): IA 1040 Step 3 computes personal credits at $40 (enter 1 for statuses 1, 3, and 5; 2 for statuses 2 and 4), $20 per 65-or-older / blind condition, and $40 per dependent; the Step 3 total is a CREDIT against tax on line 8 — never a base reduction. exemptions ships empty; pass exemptions_count=0 and dependents_count=0. Low-income exemption (NOT modeled): filers whose Iowa taxable income plus specified add-backs is at or below $9,000 (single/MFS; $24,000 if 65+ on 12/31/25), or $13,500 (MFJ / HoH / QSS; $32,000 if 65+), owe no Iowa income tax (check the box between Steps 4 and 5); a dependent filer's threshold is $5,000; MFS also requires combined income of $13,500 or less. NEW for 2025: the federal Enhanced Deduction for Seniors is added back when testing this exemption. Cents vs whole dollars: the IA 1040 is captioned 'Enter Dollars and Cents' and computes tax to the cent; whole-dollar rounding is OPTIONAL (drop under 50 cents; 50-99 cents up — a .50 tie rounds UP, matching this op). No tax-table mandate: all filers apply the 3.8% rate (or the alternate-tax / tax-reduction worksheets). Not modeled — later lines: Iowa lump-sum tax (line 6), the Step 3 exemption credits (line 8), tuition and textbook credit (line 9), volunteer firefighter/EMS/reserve peace officer credit (line 10), the IA 126 nonresident/part-year credit, out-of-state tax credit, SCHOOL DISTRICT SURTAX and EMS surtax (Step 6 — a local percentage of the balance), the 15%-of-federal Iowa EITC (line 25), and the child and dependent care / early childhood development credits (line 24).
